LightingScene, StudioLight, Position, LightOptics, and ManualRoom are structs. arranged transforms a local scene and local light copies, then throws or returns the fully validated value. Existing tests assign only the returned value and assert the caller scene remains equal to the source for invalid final light, camera, explicit aim, and subject positions.

Camera lens, preview settings, and measured room remain copied; existing full-scene equality assertions cover these properties.

ManualRoom subjectX/subjectZ are room-relative placements. Room mapping subtracts scene.subject horizontally and adds those saved room offsets; preserving room settings during scene relocation is consistent with this definition. Vertical positions remain heights above the floor, so an arrangement height change moves the equipment relative to unchanged floor/ceiling measurements.

checks.observation: Finite Kelvin is restricted to the inclusive 1000...20000 range. The fixed visible wavelength range and positive finite temperature bound keep the Planck denominator finite and positive. Endpoint trapezoid weights are present; the omitted constant 5 nm step cancels when dividing all channels by accumulated Y. The output is explicitly normalized by total.y after a finite-positive guard.

checks.method: Static coefficient/direction review and algebraic reasoning
checks.observation: The code computes source and D65 target cone responses with the same Bradford matrix, checks positive source responses, uses destination/source ratios, and applies the inverse after componentwise scaling. For an XYZ vector proportional to the selected blackbody white, this maps to the same scalar times D65 up to the declared inverse coefficient precision. No reversed white-balance ratio or mismatched white reference was found.

The blackbody range is inclusive 1000...20000 K; preview white balance is intentionally narrower at 2000...10000 K. Tests include neutralization at both white-balance endpoints, light-color endpoints in the extreme-settings matrix, NaN/999 K blackbody rejection, and 10001 K preview-setting rejection. No boundary inconsistency was found within the scoped files.

Each normalized blackbody is weighted by independently computed lux before summation, so incident XYZ Y tracks total lux. The 18%/1000 reference is applied after summation, and preview white balance does not modify the measured totalLux. Tests express matched-white channel equality at 2000, 2856, 5600 and 10000 K, expected neutral-card brightness, unchanged lux after white-balance changes, and mixed-color XYZ additivity.

w077.focus: BoundedFileReader task versus injected cancellation, before/after-read and EOF polling, partial-data nonpublication, resource cleanup, invalid limits, and integer-overflow safety.
w077.review_type: Remote pinned source and test review; no runtime execution

checks.result: The metadata preflight checks the current Swift task. Each read checkpoint checks Task.checkCancellation before calling the optional hook; a no-op hook does not disable an already-cancelled task. Source tests explicitly self-cancel tasks in both paths and expect CancellationError.

A checkpoint runs before each read. Following each nonempty read, the next iteration checks cancellation before any further read; EOF or an empty chunk is followed by a final checkpoint before the sole successful return. This is cooperative polling, not an assertion that the synchronous OS read itself is interruptible.

checks.case: Injected cancellation does not return partial bytes
checks.result: The accumulator stays local and there is only one success return after EOF and a final checkpoint. Hook errors propagate outside the FileHandle read-error conversion. The test throws on checkpoint three, after a first 64 KiB chunk, and asserts CancellationError and unchanged source bytes.

Immediately after successful open, FileHandle owns the descriptor with closeOnDealloc and a defer attempts close. Metadata rejection, hook throws, read errors, size rejection and successful return all unwind through this defer. There is no early successful partial-data publication or file mutation in the reader.

Negative limits and Int.max fail before open; a zero bound accepts an empty file. maximumBytes < Int.max makes maximumBytes + 1 representable. At the top of each loop contents.count is nonnegative and at most maximumBytes, keeping subtraction positive and representable; requested chunk size is at most remaining and 64 KiB, and the subsequent guard rejects any sentinel byte before another iteration. Nonnegative metadata size is bounded by maximumBytes before its Int conversion and reserveCapacity.
